headline: Liquid AI's 230M parameter model beats models 4X its size at data extraction, runs anywhere
summary: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-230M is designed for on-device agentic workflows, outperforming much larger models in data extraction while being small enough to run on smartphones and robotics.
details: Liquid AI has released LFM2.5-230M, its smallest AI language model yet, with just 230 million parameters. This model, explicitly designed for on-device agentic workflows, outperforms models more than 4X its size in data extraction benchmarks. It can run on smartphones, laptops, and robotics.

The model targets developers building lightweight data extraction pipelines and autonomous edge systems. It operates under a dual-use commercial license, free for individuals and companies under $10 million in annual revenue, requiring a paid agreement for larger corporations.

LFM2.5-230M distinguishes itself by using the LFM2 architecture to achieve high inference speeds without the massive memory overhead typical of parameter-heavy transformers. This signals a shift toward architectural efficiency over brute-force scaling in the race for local AI deployments.

The LFM2 architecture is a hybrid system, interleaving gated short-range convolutions with grouped-query attention for efficient information processing. It supports an expansive 32K context window, allowing it to ingest substantial documents or continuous streams of robotic telemetry.

The model maintains a memory footprint under 400MB. It achieves a decode speed of 213 tokens per second on a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra and 42 tokens per second on a Raspberry Pi 5, outpacing comparable small models.

Enterprises traditionally rely on rigid, rule-based ETL scripts, which are brittle and break with layout changes. The industry is shifting to "AI ETL," where machine learning infers mappings and adapts to changes automatically, structuring data from unstructured sources like PDFs or emails.

Using massive flagship models for routine data parsing is economically unviable due to high costs and latency. LFM2.5-230M provides a lightweight, cost-effective solution for automating repetitive formatting and data parsing directly on edge devices.

headline: Amazon drops OpenAI movie 'Artificial' starring Andrew Garfield, mid-production
summary: The $40 million biographical drama about Sam Altman was almost complete when Amazon's MGM Studios decided to pull the plug, sparking criticism.
details: Amazon's MGM Studios has abruptly dropped "Artificial," a $40 million biographical drama about OpenAI's Sam Altman, just as production was nearing completion. The film, directed by Luca Guadagnino, was described as "The Social Network for the AI Age" and starred Andrew Garfield as Altman.

The decision has drawn criticism, with many seeing it as Amazon attempting to appease OpenAI, a major player in the AI industry. The movie reportedly did not portray Altman in a favorable light, focusing on "The Blip" — Altman's brief firing and swift rehiring in November 2023.

Meanwhile, the intersection of AI and Hollywood continues to evolve. Google DeepMind recently announced a $75 million partnership with indie film studio A24 to develop AI tools for filmmaking, indicating a growing intertwining of tech and entertainment.

The tech industry is also facing internal challenges. Data center workers, including electricians and software engineers, are pushing back against working conditions and construction. A group of Amazon workers claims they are being investigated for advocating for regulation.

Separately, Meta paused a controversial internal system that tracked employees' keystrokes and screen activity. This decision came after the company internally leaked sensitive data from the program, adding to a series of internal crises at Meta.

In other news, talks between AI firm Anthropic and the government are reportedly improving. This positive shift is attributed to CEO Dario Amodei no longer being directly involved in the discussions, suggesting a change in leadership approach has aided relations.
